description: Actual UPSC CSE Prelims questions from past years

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Governor of a State can be removed by the President at any time without assigning any reason
2. The Governor can address, prorogue and dissolve the State Legislature
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both correct. Governor serves at 'pleasure of President' (Article 156) - no grounds needed for removal. Governor addresses first session (Art 176), prorogues and dissolves Assembly (Art 174).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question:
With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following statements:
1. An increase in Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) indicates depreciation of rupee
2. An increase in Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) indicates appreciation of rupee
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is wrong - increase in NEER indicates APPRECIATION (rupee strengthened). Statement 2 correct - increase in REER indicates real appreciation (adjusting for inflation differentials). REER accounts for both nominal exchange rate and relative price levels.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Biodiversity hotspots are located only in tropical regions
2. India has four biodiversity hotspots
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 wrong - hotspots exist in temperate regions too (Mediterranean Basin, California Floristic Province). Statement 2 correct - India has 4 hotspots: Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, Indo-Burma, Sundaland (Nicobar).

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
With reference to Indian history, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The Moplah Rebellion of 1921 was a peasant revolt against landlords and British
2. The movement was initially part of Khilafat-Non-Cooperation agitation
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both correct. Moplah (Mappila) Rebellion (1921): Muslim peasants in Malabar (Kerala) rose against Hindu landlords and British. It started as part of Khilafat-Non-Cooperation Movement but took on agrarian and communal character.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following:
1. Atolls
2. Barrier Reefs
3. Fringing Reefs
Which of the above is/are found in Indian waters?
questions.explanation: All three found in India. Atolls: Lakshadweep islands are coral atolls. Barrier reefs: Gulf of Mannar has barrier reef. Fringing reefs: Andaman & Nicobar, Gulf of Kutch have fringing reefs. Coral reef types: Fringing (attached to coast), Barrier (separated by lagoon), Atoll (ring-shaped).

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
Under the Indian Constitution, which of the following is correct regarding judicial review?
1. The Supreme Court can declare laws unconstitutional
2. This power extends to both Central and State laws
3. It is part of the basic structure of the Constitution
questions.explanation: All correct. Judicial review (Articles 13, 32, 226) allows SC/HCs to declare laws unconstitutional if they violate Fundamental Rights or the Constitution. It applies to both Central and State legislation. SC in many cases (L. Chandra Kumar) held judicial review as basic structure.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Which of the following is/are the application(s) of nanotechnology?
1. Targeted drug delivery
2. Water purification
3. Food packaging
questions.explanation: All three are nanotechnology applications. Targeted drug delivery: nanoparticles carry drugs to specific cells (cancer treatment). Water purification: nano-filters remove contaminants. Food packaging: nanocomposites improve shelf life, antimicrobial properties, barrier performance.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question:
With reference to 'Financial Stability and Development Council' (FSDC) in India:
1. It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister
2. It monitors macroprudential supervision of the economy
3. FSDC sub-committee is chaired by the Governor of RBI
questions.explanation: All correct. FSDC: apex body for financial stability, chaired by FM. Functions include macroprudential supervision, inter-regulatory coordination, financial literacy. Sub-committee chaired by RBI Governor deals with day-to-day coordination among regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDA, PFRDA).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question:
Which of the following Protected Areas are located in cauvery basin?
1. Nagarhole National Park
2. Papikonda National Park
3. Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve
4. Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary
questions.explanation: Nagarhole (Karnataka), Sathyamangalam (Tamil Nadu), and Wayanad (Kerala) are in the Cauvery basin. Papikonda National Park is in Andhra Pradesh on the banks of river Godavari, NOT Cauvery basin.

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
With reference to Rowlatt Act:
1. It authorized the government to imprison any person without trial
2. It was passed despite unanimous opposition from Indian members
3. It led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
questions.explanation: All correct. Rowlatt Act (March 1919): allowed detention without trial, no appeal/vakeel/daleel. Passed despite all Indian members of Imperial Legislative Council opposing. Protest against it led to Jallianwala Bagh massacre (April 13, 1919).

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
Which of the following are not provisions of the Constitution?
1. The procedure for impeachment of the President
2. The minimum age for contesting Lok Sabha elections
3. The number of judges in the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: The number of Supreme Court judges is NOT fixed in the Constitution - it is determined by Parliament through legislation (originally 8, now 34 including CJI). Impeachment procedure (Art 61) and minimum age for LS (Art 84 - 25 years) ARE in the Constitution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs:
Peak - Mountain Range
1. Nanda Devi - Garhwal Himalayas
2. Kangchenjunga - Eastern Himalayas
3. K2 - Karakoram Range
Which are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All correct. Nanda Devi (7816m, 2nd highest in India) is in Garhwal Himalayas, Uttarakhand. Kangchenjunga (8586m, 3rd highest globally) is in Eastern Himalayas (Sikkim-Nepal border). K2/Godwin-Austen (8611m, 2nd highest globally) is in Karakoram Range (PoK).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In the context of Indian economy, 'Demographic Dividend' refers to:
options: Higher GDP growth due to population increase
Increase in population density in urban areas
Higher per capita income due to technology
questions.explanation: Demographic dividend refers to economic growth potential from a population's age structure shift - when working-age population (15-64) exceeds non-working (dependents: children + elderly). India's window: 2005-2055 approximately. Requires investment in education, health, and job creation.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Consider the following about ISRO:
1. PSLV can carry multiple satellites in single launch
2. India has launched Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)
3. India is the first country to reach Mars orbit in first attempt
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. PSLV has launched 104 satellites in single mission (PSLV-C37, 2017). MOM/Mangalyaan launched September 2013, reached Mars orbit November 2014. India was first nation to succeed in Mars orbit insertion in its maiden attempt (also most cost-effective: ₹450 crore).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: 'Ecological Succession' refers to:
options: Replacement of one community by another at a given area over time
Migration of species from one region to another
Extinction of species due to environmental changes
Adaptation of species to new environmental conditions
questions.explanation: Ecological succession is the gradual process of change in species composition of a community over time in a given area. Types: Primary (bare/lifeless area, e.g., lava, bare rock) and Secondary (after disturbance to existing community, e.g., after fire/flood). Pioneer species → Climax community.
